architectureDecisions: Resolve delivered adapters through AGENT_TOOLS with a minimal capability contract rather than growing another hard-coded tool list. Pin the BB-122 delivered adapter at Worker start.
Keep provider/auth/model inputs explicit; fixture tests do not call a model. Do not require Codex/Kiro/agy installation to exercise a supported local Grok/OpenCode path.

Replace the SLICE_TOOLS id whitelist with a no-spawn capability probe in packages/agent-tools/src/deliver-slice.js: probeDeliverCapability(tool) calls tool.buildInvocation with the exact deliver request shape {prompt, resume: null, model: null, permissionProfile: 'WORKSPACE_EDIT', logFile, promptFile, cwd, timeoutMs} and again with resume: {sessionRef: 'probe-session'}, then checks tool.parseResult({exitCode: 0, stdout: ''}) returns the {claimedSuccess, finalMessage, sessionRef} tuple. validateDeliverSlice accepts exactly the AGENT_TOOLS ids whose probe succeeds (codex, kiro, agy, grok, opencode at the contract baseline) and throws TypeError before any spawn otherwise. Missing binaries still fail through resolveExecutable to TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with reason NOT_INSTALLED; a tool-mismatched resume throws RecoveryError TOOL_MISMATCH in resumeSupervisedTask before spawn; a non-sha acceptance yields QA_FAILED with INVALID_ACCEPTED_SHA. None of these paths can fabricate ACCEPTED.

researchEvidence.finding: EXECUTED no-spawn probe 2026-10-01 (local node, zero provider calls, zero spawns): called buildInvocation on every AGENT_TOOLS entry with the exact deliver request shape {prompt, resume, model:null, permissionProfile:'WORKSPACE_EDIT', logFile, promptFile, cwd, timeoutMs:1} for resume:null and resume:{sessionRef:'probe-session'}, then parseResult({exitCode:0, stdout:''}). All five adapters built argv without throwing and returned the {claimedSuccess, finalMessage, sessionRef} tuple. Argv per adapter — codex fresh: `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -` (prompt on stdin), resume: `codex exec resume probe-session --json -`; kiro fresh: `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive --trust-tools=fs_read,fs_write probe`, resume adds `--resume`; agy fresh: `agy --print probe --mode accept-edits --print-timeout 1s --log-file probe.log`, resume adds `--continue`; grok fresh: `grok --output-format json --model grok-4.6 --cwd probe-cwd --permission-mode acceptEdits --disable-web-search --no-subagents --no-auto-update --prompt-file probe.prompt`, resume adds `--resume probe-session`; opencode fresh: `opencode run --format json --dir probe-cwd -- probe`, resume adds `--session probe-session`. parseResult tuples: all {claimedSuccess:true, finalMessage:null, sessionRef:null}. Conclusion: grok and opencode satisfy the same headless/edit/resume contract as the three deliver-admitted tools; the only deliver exclusion is the SLICE_TOOLS id whitelist. The deliver Backend path (runSupervisedTask) is tool-agnostic beyond this contract: the supervisor supplies logFile, promptFile, cwd and timeoutMs to every invocation, which are exactly the extra fields agy (logFile/timeoutMs) and grok (promptFile) require.

DELIVERED_TRUTH: AGENT_TOOLS is frozen {codex, kiro, agy, grok, opencode} under AGENT_TOOL_ADAPTER_V1. Every adapter passes assertInvocationRequest: non-empty prompt, resume null|{sessionRef}, model null|string, permissionProfile in WORKSPACE_EDIT|FULL_AUTO. grokTool builds --output-format json --model <model|grok-4.6> [--cwd] [--always-approve | --permission-mode acceptEdits] [--resume <sessionRef> | --continue] --prompt-file; parseResult reads the first balanced JSON object for sessionId/text and returns claimedSuccess=(exitCode===0). opencodeTool builds run --format json [--dir cwd] [--model] [--auto for FULL_AUTO] [--session <id> | --continue] -- <prompt>; parseResult extracts sessionID and the last text part from JSONL, same {claimedSuccess, finalMessage, sessionRef} shape.

DELIVERED_TRUTH: every agent invocation request is {prompt, resume, model, permissionProfile, logFile, promptFile, cwd: root} with promptFile written next to the attempt log outside the worktree. Grok's promptFile requirement and OpenCode's --dir cwd are therefore always satisfied on the deliver Backend path without manifest changes.

DELIVERED_TRUTH: SLICE_TOOLS=[codex,kiro,agy]; validateDeliverSlice throws TypeError 'tool must be one of codex|kiro|agy' before any process starts, so an unknown tool can never reach ACCEPTED. resolveSliceTool returns null when AGENT_TOOLS lacks the id or resolveExecutable misses the binary; the slice then returns TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with reason NOT_INSTALLED. A mismatched recovery handle throws RecoveryError HANDLE_INVALID before resume/QA/dispose; a non-40-hex acceptance yields QA_FAILED with INVALID_ACCEPTED_SHA. Missing-binary and invalid-acceptance paths never fabricate ACCEPTED. The planned replacement is a no-spawn capability probe (buildInvocation over the exact deliver request shape for resume null and resume {sessionRef}, plus the parseResult tuple check); validateDeliverSlice will accept exactly the AGENT_TOOLS ids whose probe succeeds.
